The highest-transfer analogue (0.8157) shows only 24% brain penetration relative to plasma in rat, making it the strongest individual anchor because it combines the highest transfer score with a direct systemic brain-penetration measurement. The experimental result therefore outweighs any more favorable physicochemical intuition: whatever mechanism limits its CNS exposure is real. Because the transfer score is high and the query shares relevant ionization and heteroatom features, that measured phenotype has strong implications for the query.

The next three analogues have closely matched transfer scores (0.7874, 0.7855, and 0.7800) and independently support the same direction. The pattern continues at 0.7708 and 0.7603, where biodistribution and brain-to-blood measurements again show poor CNS exposure.
